name: Ninja
listed_description: Alternative build generator target that CMake can emit build files for, selected with -G Ninja; the book notes it uses all available hardware threads by default.
claim_text: Book gives no timing for Ninja; it only says Ninja tries to use as many hardware threads as available, so a job count is redundant.
found_in: book: CMake Best Practices (2024), ch. 1, section Understanding the CMake build process; ch. 2, Building in parallel

name: CMake parallel build job count (cmake --build --parallel N)
listed_description: Timing of the same small example project built with one job versus more jobs via the --parallel option, to show build-time scaling.
claim_text: Even on a very simple project, extra jobs clearly give faster build times; results are shown only as screenshots.
book_benchmark: time tool on a small example project, --parallel 1 versus --parallel 4; Ubuntu 22.04, Intel 11th Gen laptop CPU at 2.5 GHz, 32 GB RAM; numbers only in figures 2.14 and 2.15, not in text.
found_in: book: CMake Best Practices (2024), ch. 2, section Using CMake via a command-line interface, Building in parallel
